title: The National Action Movement (Movimiento de Acción Nacional, MAN), the political party of Gustavo Rojas Pinilla, is created.

title: The 1955 Vuelta a Colombia ends, Ramón Hoyos comes in first place overall.
text: Ramón Hoyos Vallejo was a Colombian road bicycle racer who won the men's individual road race at the 1959 Pan American Games. He represented his native country twice at the Summer Olympics; in 1956 and 1960.

title: The newspaper El Tiempo is closed.
text: El Tiempo is a Colombian newspaper founded on January 30, 1911, by Alfonso Villegas Restrepo. It is currently the newspaper with the largest circulation in Colombia and for seven years was practically the only one with national circulation, due to the crisis of its main competitor, El Espectador, which became a weekly in 2001 but returned to daily publication in 2008.

title: Independiente Medellín wins the 1955 Campeonato Profesional.
text: Deportivo Independiente Medellín, also known as Independiente Medellín or DIM, is a Colombian professional football club based in Medellín that currently plays in the Categoría Primera A. They play their home games at Estadio Atanasio Girardot, which seats 40,943 people, and is also shared with city rivals Atlético Nacional. title: Rojas Pinilla orders a military offensive against rearmed peasants, triggering a confrontation known as the "Guerra de Villarrica" (War of Villarrica) which took place in the central town of Villarrica in Tolima Department.
text: Tolima is one of the 32 departments of Colombia, located in the Andean region, in the center-west of the country. It is bordered on the north and the west by the department of Caldas; on the east by the department of Cundinamarca; on the south by the department of Huila, and on the west by the departments of Cauca, Valle del Cauca, Quindío and Risaralda.
